_meta.title: Down the Rabbit-Hole
_meta.language: English (project output language; every prompt_terms string is written to be quoted verbatim into a video or image prompt)
_meta.scope: One episode's shooting grammar: the lens set and what each focal length is for, the camera height that carries each of Alice's four scale states, the colour temperature of every light in the episode keyed to the controlled time_of_day vocabulary, the depth-of-field policy, and the texture/finish wording. NOT in scope and not written here: per-shot camera moves (07-directing/camera-movement), per-shot composition and framing (07-directing/composition), the film-wide style (06-art/art-director, H2-locked), the grade and the finish pass (Phase 9).

directing/ep01/storyboard.json (draft; read only to see which situations actually occur - the shot list and the group split are NOT treated as final)

Where the directing plan and an amended Bible file disagree, the Bible wins and the disagreement is listed in conflicts[].
_meta.one_line_thesis: Nine feet and ten inches are the same girl in the same room; only the lens height and the gauge in the frame tell the audience which. Everything else in this episode is shot plainly, on three prime lenses, so that the four rationed exceptions land.

format.generation_resolution: 480p draft, finished by upscale to 1080p (bible/aspect_ratio.json). Consequence for this file: every texture and optical instruction below is specified at the scale of the frame, never at the scale of the pixel.
format.focal_length_convention: All focal lengths in this file are 35 mm full-frame equivalents, i.e. a statement about field of view. Write them into prompts exactly as given ('shot on a 40 mm lens'). Do NOT convert them, do not halve them for anamorphic squeeze, and do not translate them into sensor-specific numbers.
format.anamorphic_ruling: style.json says '35mm film with anamorphic lenses'. In ep01 that word is a FINISH, not a field-of-view instruction: mildly oval highlights, a faint horizontal flare on the lamp flames, gentle halation. It never means a stretched or squeezed frame, and it never changes a focal number in this file. The style fragment carries the word; no shot-level prompt needs to repeat it.

lens_set.principle: ep01 is shot as if on one small set of primes, so that ninety-odd shots made in parallel read as one photographer's work. Three lenses do 95 % of the episode; two more are rationed to single uses and are what the audience remembers without knowing why.

working_primes.role: space and bulk. The lens that can say 'this hall is 32 m long and only 2.8 m high' in one frame, and the lens that makes a giant overflow the frame while the far end of the same room stays tiny. Also every deep-staged waking wide.
the human-eye lens. Travelling mediums, POV, two-plane cause-and-effect inserts, and the Rabbit at water level. Six of the episode's seven POVs are 40 mm.
faces, hands and hero objects. The longest lens permitted in the waking frame, and the only lens allowed on a face at close range at ANY of Alice's four scales.

spent_on: S06 - straight up the glass table leg from the flagstones (tiny scale)
S07 - straight down her own body to her feet far below (giant scale)
rationed.role: The two purely vertical scale axes of the episode, and nothing else. 24 mm exaggerates near-to-far along the axis of the shot, which is exactly what those two images are for. Dream register only.
rationed.rule: Any other request for 24 mm in ep01 is refused: it is the lens that would start to look like a fisheye distortion of a child's body, which CR-011 forbids.

spent_on: S05 - her POV down the crawl passage to the garden arch
rationed.role: The episode's one long lens. It flattens the garden into an unreachable postcard: the goal must look like a keyhole, not a place we could walk into (directing_plan S05).
rationed.rule: Dream register only, once. This is the only shot in ep01 where the camera tells the audience something untrue about distance - which is precisely the feeling of the scene. It must not be reused for a second 'nice' compression anywhere.

lens_set.register_separator: The waking frame (S01, S02) is shot on 28 / 40 / 50 only. 24 mm and 100 mm are dream lenses. This is the same register discipline CR-014 applies to ornament, carried by the lens: nothing leaks across the hedge.
banned_optics_ep01: fisheye and any visible barrel distortion (CR-011)
macro / tilt-shift / miniature-diorama optics - see dof_policy MINIATURE-LOOK BAN
zoom moves of any kind (a zoom is not in the film's in-camera vocabulary, CR-006)

focal_rules.occurs_at: S01 the opening meadow wide, the sleeping-profile wide across to the far spire, the rabbit's pass; S02 the wide from the burrow mouth back across the field
focal_rules.note: Deep-staged, low in the grass: seed-heads across the bottom of frame, the girls small and central, the far elms and spire still readable. The rabbit's pass has to hold Alice's shoes AND the animal in one unbroken frame, which only a wide can do without heroing him.
prompt_terms: shot on a 28 mm lens, camera low in the long meadow grass
deep staging: seed-heads and grass stems crossing the bottom of frame, the figures small and central, the far trees and spire still readable

focal_rules.occurs_at: the tracking pass alongside her through the grass; the arrival at the hedge foot
focal_rules.note: The lens that keeps her, the grass streaking past and the hedge in one honest space. Mild handheld is licensed here and only here (directing_plan 2); the move itself belongs to camera-movement, this rule only fixes the lens.
prompt_terms: shot on a 40 mm lens at hip height, moving alongside her
grass whipping through the near foreground, the hedge line held in the background

focal_rules.occurs_at: S01 the low medium-close past the open book, her flushed profile with the daisy, the eyes closing; S02 her cheek and one eye against the black burrow mouth
focal_rules.note: 50 mm is the LONGEST lens allowed anywhere in S01-S02: the waking frame is plain period realism with no long-lens compression (directing_plan 5). Where a face shares the frame with a landmark (the burrow oval), keep the face off the frame edge so nothing stretches.
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens, camera lying on the grass at the child's eye-line
out-of-focus grass stems crossing the near foreground, her face and the near ground sharp

focal_rules.occurs_at: the insert of the sister's open book: close grey print, margin to margin, no picture (POV 1 of 7)
focal_rules.lens_height_m: about 0.30 above the book, slightly off square so the page takes no glare
focal_rules.note: Her POV, so it takes the human-eye lens. The page reads as a page, not as a macro texture.
prompt_terms: shot on a 40 mm lens, looking down at an open book from a child's eye-line
close grey printed text filling the frame margin to margin, no illustration, no glare on the paper

focal_rules.occurs_at: the locked wide from the shaft wall where she holds one place in frame while the dressing travels up past her; the same set-up returns at 'Down, down, down'
focal_rules.lens_height_m: on her own axis in a 2.4 m shaft; no horizon
focal_rules.note: The wide is what makes the shaft a volume and the fall endless. The hook and the S03 return are the SAME lens on the SAME axis - that is what lets the audience recognise the image instead of re-watching it (directing_plan anti-repeat rule).
prompt_terms: shot on a 28 mm lens, locked off, the camera falling with her so she holds one place in frame
the shaft walls and their dressing travelling upward past her, no horizon, no tilt

focal_rules.occurs_at: her POV down the open centre of the shaft into black, used twice (POV 3 and 4 of 7) - identical set-up both times, only the wall dressing differs
focal_rules.lens_height_m: on her axis at the middle of the shaft
focal_rules.note: Identical focal on both uses. If the second POV is shot on a different lens the repetition stops reading as the same thought returning.
prompt_terms: shot on a 40 mm lens looking straight down the open centre of a deep shaft
the nearest wall bands just readable, the depth below falling away into total black

focal_rules.occurs_at: the marmalade jar held out over the drop; the profile close as she settles with her hair floating up; the eyes closing and the two-second hold
focal_rules.lens_height_m: beside her, at her own height
focal_rules.note: The one unbroken shot where the dream begins has to be a plain 50 mm profile - the audience must be able to point at the frame, and any optical event would do the announcing the whole design forbids.
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens, camera beside her at her own height, drifting with her
her hair floating upward, the shelf dressing travelling up through the background

focal_rules.occurs_at: every shot of the White Rabbit in S04: the wide down the long low passage, the medium-wide as he reads the watch, the medium past the mosaic dado to the lit corner
focal_rules.note: The distance to the Rabbit must be REAL distance, never a long lens pretending. A deep-staged 28 mm keeps him small, in profile and far down the vault, which is the cheapest insurance against the uncanny and honours the waived character sheet (directing_plan S04). Never come closer than medium-wide on him in this scene, and never bring him closer by changing lens.
prompt_terms: shot on a 28 mm lens down the length of a long low brick-vaulted passage
the animal genuinely far away and in profile, small in the frame, the vault receding behind him

focal_rules.occurs_at: the one insert of the watch face and the paw (his face is spent once, in S08, not here)
focal_rules.note: Read the watch on the dial, not on his face. A 50 mm at close focus keeps the fur and the enamel in the same world; a macro would turn it into a product shot.
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens at close focus on the enamel watch dial and the paw holding it
warm lamplight on the enamel, the chain and the fur sharp, the passage behind falling off into soft dark

focal_rules.occurs_at: the single hall reveal; the wide down the hall under the lamp row; the twelve-second locked wide that covers the shrink; the wide at the foot of the table leg; the held wide that covers the growth
focal_rules.lens_height_m: 1.20-1.35 at normal size; per scale_lens_map at every other size
focal_rules.note: 28 mm is the only lens that states the hall's two facts at once - 32 m long, 2.80 m to the vault crown, lamps at 2.30 m, doors at 1.95 m (architecture.json; whitebox gauges). Every size beat is covered by this lens held still, so the change lives in the set and not in the optics (CR-005).
prompt_terms: shot on a 28 mm lens, the long low vaulted hall running away from camera
the whole height of the low vault and the hanging lamp row inside the frame, the far end lost in darkness

focal_rules.occurs_at: the door round along the west wall and its failing return pass (S05); two-foot Alice running the same wall (S09)
focal_rules.note: MATCH PAIR. Same lens, same axis, different height: the wall takes three times as long to pass because she is a third of the size, and the audience feels the hall repeat. If S09 is shot on a different focal length the structural joke of the episode dies.
prompt_terms: shot on a 40 mm lens, travelling with her along the row of locked oak doors
iron handles and horseshoe-arched door frames passing through frame at a steady rate

focal_rules.occurs_at: her hand on the iron handle and her face at a locked door; the return to her face lit by the garden; the bottle held at arm's length; the three tastings
focal_rules.note: Child height, never adult height (CR-011, directing_plan camera-height law).
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens at the child's own eye height
her face held whole in frame, the dim hall soft behind her

focal_rules.occurs_at: her POV through the 0.38 m door, down the crawl passage, to the garden arch (POV 5 of 7)
focal_rules.note: The episode's only long lens, spent here. The compression flattens the passage so the garden sits small and flat at the end of it like a postcard - a keyhole, not a place we could walk into. No rack focus and no defocus in this shot: the flatness must come from the lens alone (see dof_policy).
prompt_terms: shot on a 100 mm lens looking down a long, narrow stone crawl passage
the small sunlit garden arch at the far end sitting flat and small in the frame, compressed and unreachable

focal_rules.occurs_at: the reveal of ten-inch Alice beside the bottle at the mosaic dado; the three climbing attempts at the foot of the leg; the wide of her alone in the enormous hall; the crossing of the flag joints to the glass box
focal_rules.lens_height_m: 0.15-0.25 (at or below her own 0.22 m eye-line)
focal_rules.note: The default lens of the ten-inch state. It works only when a gauge sits within ~0.3 m of the lens - the DRINK ME bottle at her exact height, the mosaic dado border, a flagstone joint, the base of a glass leg - so the near-to-far ratio does the shrinking. A gauge in the near foreground is the price of using 28 mm here.
prompt_terms: shot on a 28 mm lens, camera on the flagstones below her own eye height
a near-foreground object at her exact height in the same frame, the hall towering away behind her, the low vault far above

focal_rules.occurs_at: straight up the glass table leg from the flagstones, the tabletop a glass ceiling with the golden key visible through it (1 of the 2 rationed 24 mm shots)
focal_rules.note: Goal and obstacle in one set-up - the episode's thesis. 24 mm because the whole image is a near-to-far exaggeration up a single vertical axis.
prompt_terms: shot on a 24 mm lens looking straight up a tall clear glass table leg from floor level
the glass tabletop reading as a ceiling overhead with a tiny gold key visible through it

focal_rules.occurs_at: the one earned close-up at the foot of the leg where she scolds herself; the bite and the hand; the held flat cheated face
focal_rules.note: HARD RULE: never a wide lens on a face at the ten-inch scale. A 28 mm close to a child's face stretches it, and a stretched child's face is the exact failure mode style.json bans ('cartoon animal face', 'distorted face', CR-001). The room has already done the scale work in the shot before; the face shot only has to be a face.
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens at close focus, camera on the flagstones
her face held whole and undistorted, natural facial proportions, the flagstones and the hall soft behind her

focal_rules.occurs_at: the bent neck and shoulder against the vault; the hand, knee and bent back crossing the frame; the wall of blue cotton and one knee at water level; the enormous hand coming down into the top of the frame
focal_rules.note: At 2.74 m in a 2.80 m room she can never be framed standing, so the widescreen frame becomes the cage: the 28 mm lets her bulk run out of frame in both directions while the far end of the same hall stays tiny in the same image. That simultaneity IS the size beat - going long would lose the room and with it the comparison.
prompt_terms: shot on a 28 mm lens, camera low on the stone floor
part of her body filling and overflowing the frame, the far end of the hall small and dark in the same image

focal_rules.occurs_at: the look down her own body to her feet far below on the flagstones - 'Good-bye, feet!' (2 of the 2 rationed 24 mm shots)
focal_rules.lens_height_m: at her own eye height near the lamp line, aimed straight down
focal_rules.note: The one piece of pure comedy in the dream half, and it is an optical joke: the 24 mm stretches the body axis so the boots are absurdly far away. It is also the last set-up in the episode allowed to sit near the lamp line.
prompt_terms: shot on a 24 mm lens looking straight down the length of her own body to her feet far below on the stone floor
her boots small and distant at the bottom of the frame, the body running away steeply down the middle of the image

focal_rules.occurs_at: the giant lying on her side, one eye at the 0.38 m doorway with garden light across it - the image the climax then breaks
focal_rules.note: 50 mm so the eye stays anatomically true and the 0.38 m opening keeps its real size. A wide here would bend the eye and the arch and turn the best image in the episode into an effect.
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens flat across the stone floor
one enormous human eye at a tiny 38 cm horseshoe-arched doorway, the eye undistorted and anatomically real, the dark mass of her body running out of frame both ways

focal_rules.occurs_at: his approach out of the dark between the lamp pools; the clean single on him as he mutters; the two-step look up that runs out of room
focal_rules.note: The human-eye lens on him for the same reason as S04: no optical flattery. This is the shot where the CGI either works or it does not, so the evidence must be photographic - displaced water, wet leg fur, ripples starting under his feet, exact eyeline (CR-015). His face is spent here, once.
prompt_terms: shot on a 40 mm lens with the lens right on the water surface, the waterline cutting across the frame
real displaced water and ripples starting under his feet, wet fur on his legs, his reflection doubled on the flooded stone

focal_rules.occurs_at: the identity aria: one sustained set-up on her face, returned to exactly, broken only for her hands
focal_rules.note: Her head is within reach of a water-level 50 mm only because the POSE brings it down - hunched, wet-faced, folded into a room too low for her. The lens does not solve the geometry and must not be asked to: no long lens reaching up at her, because that would put the 2.30 m lamp line and the vault in frame and break act 5's 'lamps out of frame' rule. Same focal on every return so the aria reads as one continuous thing.
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens, camera at water level on the flooded flagstones
her face held whole in the frame, lit only by broken reflected light off the water, the hall behind her almost black

focal_rules.occurs_at: her open hands as she counts the arithmetic, her fingers as long as the fan; the gloves and fan hitting the water; the white kid glove that now simply fits
focal_rules.note: The glove that fits is the episode's one image, and it is an insert, not an effect. 50 mm at close focus, with a known gauge in the frame (the fan, the wrist, the water line) so the size reads without a word.
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens at close focus, camera at water level
the object and her hand sharp together in one frame, dark water and broken amber reflections behind

focal_rules.occurs_at: the look up into the dark vault as she asks for her family - the only up-angle in the whole episode
focal_rules.note: Wide, not long: the shot has to show the black above her as a VOLUME she is asking into. It is also the one licensed exception to the act-5 rule, and it works only because the vault above her is unlit - a wider lens here brings in more darkness, not more lamp (and no lamp fixture may enter the frame).
prompt_terms: shot on a 28 mm lens, camera low on the wet flagstones tilted up past her face
an enormous unlit vault of darkness above her filling the top of the frame, no light fitting anywhere in shot

focal_rules.occurs_at: movement 4: the fan still moving in her hand while the table edge visibly rises past frame behind it; the fan leaves her hand and the rising stops in the same frame
focal_rules.note: With narration off, the picture alone carries the cause. Both planes must be legible at once, so this is a 40 mm at deep focus and never a rack (see dof_policy). The reference axis is deliberately the one used all through S06, so the comparison lands against a frame the audience already knows.
prompt_terms: shot on a 40 mm lens, deep focus, the moving fan in the near foreground and the table edge behind it both sharp in the same frame
no focus change during the shot

focal_rules.occurs_at: the stamped foot in the puddle; her chin almost in the water as she talks to herself; the realisation on the drifting fan; both lines whole in one shot
focal_rules.lens_height_m: 0.05-0.20, just above the surface, never above
focal_rules.note: The camera is in the water with her for the whole of S10 and never rises above the waterline - there is no rescuing god's-eye in this episode (directing_plan S10; this also rules out any high or crane view).
prompt_terms: shot on a 50 mm lens with the lens just above the water surface, the waterline cutting low across the frame
her face close and whole, broken warm reflections crossing the dark water behind her

focal_rules.occurs_at: the flooded hall as a canyon - door bases as cliffs, glass table legs as columns, the far shore steps; her swim toward the brightest water (POV 7 of 7)
focal_rules.note: The canyon is a scale statement, so it takes the space lens with the surface itself as the near-foreground gauge. The mosaic shimmering just under the surface is the one texture allowed to read here.
prompt_terms: shot on a 28 mm lens with the lens on the water surface, looking down the length of a flooded stone hall
door bases rising like cliffs and glass table legs standing like columns out of the water, pastel-and-gold mosaic shimmering just under the surface

focal_rules.occurs_at: the last image of the episode: a single V-wake crossing the broken lamplight toward camera, its maker never breaking the surface
focal_rules.note: Human-eye lens, practical water only, no creature asset and nothing lit from under the water. The dread is entirely in what the frame does not contain, so nothing optical may hint at a subject.
prompt_terms: shot on a 40 mm lens, camera static with the lens right on the water surface
a single V-shaped wake travelling toward camera across broken warm reflections on black water, nothing visible above or below the surface

scale_lens_map.why: Alice changes scale three times inside one room (S06 drink, S07 cake, S08 fan). CR-005 forbids showing a transformation, so the lens and the camera height are where the audience reads her size - and this table is the only place a downstream prompt can get that from.

gauges.source: bible/scenes/SCN-long-hall/whitebox.json via directing_plan (decision 2); architecture.json gives the hall as ~32 m x 5.5 m
gauges.binding_rule: Every size beat shows Alice against at least TWO gauges inside one frame (directing_plan). A gauge that is out of focus is not a gauge - see dof_policy.

states.reads_as_normal_because: the lens sits at HER height, so nothing is exaggerated; the doors at 1.95 m are a little taller than she is and the vault is barely above an adult's reach.
prompt_terms: camera at the child's own eye height, about 1.3 m above the stone floor
the oak doors a little taller than she is, the hanging lamps just above head height

states.lens_height_m: 0.15-0.25, i.e. at or below her own 0.22 m eye-line - the camera is down on the flagstones with her for every shot of this state
states.reads_as_small_because: a wide lens sits on the floor within ~0.3 m of an object of KNOWN size at her exact height - the DRINK ME bottle, a flagstone joint, the mosaic dado border - while the 2.80 m vault and the 2.30 m lamp row tower away in the same frame. She is the same height as the bottle she just drank from; that comparison does more than any effect shot.
prompt_terms: camera on the stone floor, about 0.2 m above it, looking slightly up
the empty bottle standing beside her at exactly her own height in the near foreground
the glass table looming overhead like a ceiling, the vault and hanging lamps far above
an oversized practical set built to this scale, photographed in one continuous angle - no transformation, no morph, no glow
forbidden: a wide lens close to her face

states.lens_height_m: 0.30-1.00 and NEVER above 1.00. From the first frame of S08 the camera is below 1.00 m and stays there for the rest of the episode.
states.reads_as_giant_because: we keep the ROOM's viewpoint, not hers. The lens stays on the floor, she overflows a frame that still contains the far end of the hall, and the gauges come to meet her in sequence: the table sinks to her knee (0.715 m), the lamps come down to her shoulder (2.30 m), her head meets an iron rib of the vault (2.80 m). At 2.74 m in a 2.80 m room she can never be framed standing - every giant frame is a hunch, a lie-down or a fragment.
states.act5_binding_rule: color_script act 5 requires the lamps OUT OF FRAME while her head is above the 2.30 m lamp line. The only way both are true is a camera under 1.00 m. The last set-up in the episode allowed to contain a lamp fixture is the S07 vault-knock; from S08 shot 1 no lamp fitting enters any frame.
prompt_terms: camera low on the stone floor, well under a metre, looking across at her
the glass table only knee-high to her, the hanging lamps at her shoulder, her head against an iron rib of the low vault
part of her filling and overflowing the frame while the far end of the hall stays small in the same image
no light fitting anywhere in frame

states.lens_height_m: 0.50-0.60 on dry stone (S09); 0.05-0.15 above the water surface in S10, never above the waterline
states.reads_as_small_because: repetition, not exaggeration. The same 40 mm travelling set-up as the S05 door round, now at 0.55 m, so the same wall takes three times as long to pass; the 0.715 m table is now a high shelf with the key a spark on top of it; in the flood every measurement is taken against door bases and table legs.
prompt_terms: camera at about 0.55 m, travelling with her along the same row of locked doors
the glass table now above her head like a high shelf, the tiny gold key a spark on top of it
lens just above the water surface at her swimming height, the waterline cutting low across the frame
forbidden: any high, crane or drone view over the pool (directing_plan S10 - there is no rescuing god's-eye in this episode)

pair: S09 the run for the little door
match_focal_pairs.why: the hall must repeat; the size is the only variable

pair: S06 the floor axis from the curtain to the glass table
S08 movement 4, she is small again
match_focal_pairs.changes: nothing but her height in the frame
match_focal_pairs.why: the comparison lands against a frame the audience already knows

pair: S03 POV down the shaft, first use
S03 POV down the shaft, second use
match_focal_pairs.why: the same thought returning, not a new shot

pov_lens_rule.rule: ep01 has exactly seven POVs (directing_plan 3). Six are 40 mm, the human-eye lens: the pictureless page (S01), the dark of the burrow (S02), straight down the shaft twice (S03), the key through the tabletop glass (S06), the flooded canyon (S10). The seventh, the garden down the crawl passage (S05), is 100 mm.
pov_lens_rule.why: POV means desire, and desire is normally honest here. The garden is the one thing she cannot have, so it is the one POV that lies about distance. Keeping the other six at 40 mm is what makes that single lie legible.

vocabulary.source: ENV-ENUM-v1 / LGT-ENUM-v1 (runs/p3-lighting-sb1/result.json shared_conventions), the controlled time_of_day set this project's scene Bible uses

color_temp_buckets.neutral (~4500K): about 3500-5800 K, which includes the 1862 afternoon sun at about 5000-5400 K

vocabulary.bucket_vs_number: A lighting card's color_temp string is a BUCKET NAME; its kelvin_approx is the design number. Where the two look different (e.g. SCN-riverbank: 'neutral (~4500K)' with kelvin_approx 5400) there is no conflict - quote the number, not the bucket.
vocabulary.kelvin_in_prompts: Kelvin is written into a prompt only for an actual light SOURCE. The cool ambience of the dream is carried by named palette colours (verdigris teal, slate grey, soot shadow), never by a negative Kelvin figure. The grade shifts in color_script (dream -300 K, act 2 -150 K, act 5 -400 K) belong to color-script and the grade pass and must NEVER appear in a prompt.

absent_in_ep01.afternoon: N/A - does not occur in ep01
absent_in_ep01.late_afternoon: N/A - does not occur in ep01. BINDING CONSEQUENCE: SCN-long-hall scheme LGT-long-hall-02 and SCN-little-door-passage scheme LGT-little-door-passage-02 are both late_afternoon (the ch007 return) and are OUT OF BOUNDS for this episode. No ep01 scene entry carries a late-afternoon or low-sun descriptor.

'Lit roundel' here means front-lit by a nearby lamp; nothing is lit from behind, and there are no glass pools on the floor (see conflicts[0]).

Lamps OUT OF FRAME. The lowest luma of the episode; the blind roundels go dark with the lamps. The only light accent is small dim broken specular flecks of the off-frame lamps on the tear water - never a pool of light, never on Alice, the walls or the vault, under ~5 % of frame. Camera is a raking water-level lens, which multiplies specular area, so keep the flecks in the FAR THIRD of the shot and never under her (directing_plan risk flag). Alice's cornflower blue is the only colour left.

dof_policy.rule: THE EPISODE'S FIRST DEPTH RULE: every size beat is deep focus, and no gauge may be defocused. A size beat is a frame that compares Alice with at least two of the fixed gauges; if one of them is soft the comparison is not made and the shot has failed. This also covers the S08 movement-4 chain (fan still moving in the near foreground WHILE the table edge rises behind it), where both planes are the whole point.
prompt_terms: deep focus: the near-foreground object and the far end of the hall both sharp in the same frame

dof_policy.rule: Shallow depth of field at close range on a small subject is the visual signature of PHOTOGRAPHING A MINIATURE. Used on ten-inch or two-foot Alice it would make the oversized practical set read as a toy and destroy the whole size grammar (CR-005) and the photographed-live-action finish (CR-001). Tiny scale therefore takes deep focus and an ordinary perspective, always.

super_resolution_discipline.why: Video is generated at 480p and finished by upscaling (bible/aspect_ratio.json). Any texture that only exists at the pixel level is either absent from the draft or invented by the upscaler, and in both cases it is not under anyone's control.
super_resolution_discipline.rule: Specify texture at the scale of the FRAME, not the pixel. Everything in texture[] above is a large-scale optical or atmospheric fact - bloom around a flame, haze in a volume, falloff across a wall, contrast across an image - and all of it survives a super-resolution pass. Grain is the one exception and it is handled by leaving it alone: style_fragment_ui already says 'fine film grain' and is quoted verbatim in every prompt, so no shot-level prompt adds a grain word.

handoff.camera-movement: The lens set and the camera-height law are fixed here; the moves are yours. Two constraints bite: the S08 failed tilt starts from a lens under 1.00 m and must run out of room BEFORE any lamp fixture enters frame, and the S09 travelling medium must reuse the S05 focal (40 mm) exactly or the hall stops repeating.
handoff.composition: The depth-of-field policy is the only thing here that constrains you: at every size beat both gauges must be sharp, which means both gauges must be IN the frame. The 24 mm and 100 mm shots are single-use and are listed by name in lens_set.rationed.
handoff.blocking: scale_lens_map.states gives the camera height for each of Alice's four sizes. In the aria her head is reachable by a water-level 50 mm only because she is hunched and folded - the pose has to bring her face down; the lens cannot.
handoff.08-video-gen/prompt: Quote prompt_terms verbatim. Write focal lengths exactly as given ('shot on a 40 mm lens') and do not convert them. Kelvin goes in a prompt only for a real source; the grade shifts (-300 / -150 / -400 K) never do. The forbidden_terms lists under color_temp are the daylight red line - in S04 through S10 the only daylight word permitted anywhere is the little-door garden in S05 and S07, and after S07 not even that.
handoff.continuity-planning: Three things to hold: the lamps leave frame at the start of S08 and never return; the garden daylight is spent at the S07 eye-at-the-door and does not reappear (the little door is found shut in S09); and the S05/S09 and S06/S08 match pairs must keep the same focal length across the episode or the repetitions stop reading.
